title: House Robber: Take It or Skip It, House by House
summary: At each house, the best total is the bigger of skipping it or taking it plus the best from two houses back.

takeaway.summary: best[i] = max(best[i − 1], best[i − 2] + money[i]). Each cell decides one house using two answers already in the table.
takeaway.spaceComplexity: O(n), or O(1) keeping two numbers
whenToUse: Choosing items in a row with a rule against picking neighbors
Each item is either taken or skipped

scenes.narration: A burglar works a street of five houses holding 3, 10, 4, 2, and 9. Neighbors share an alarm, so two houses side by side can't both be robbed. What's the most to take?
scenes.caption: Five houses, neighbors share an alarm: what's the most to take?

scenes.narration: Listing every allowed set of houses grows exponentially. Instead, decide one house at a time and remember the best total so far.
scenes.caption: Trying every allowed plan doubles with each house

scenes.narration: House 0 alone gives 3. At house 1, skipping keeps 3, but taking it gives 10, so the best so far is 10.
scenes.caption: House 1: take 10 instead of keeping 3

scenes.narration: Taking house 2 means skipping house 1: 3 plus 4 is 7. Skipping it keeps 10. Skip wins.
scenes.caption: House 2: 3 + 4 = 7 is less than 10, so skip it

scenes.narration: Taking house 3 adds its 2 to the best from two houses back, 10: 12 beats skipping.
scenes.caption: House 3: 10 + 2 = 12 beats 10

scenes.narration: Taking house 4 adds 9 to the best from two houses back, 10: 19, more than 12. The plan changes to houses 1 and 4.
scenes.caption: House 4: 10 + 9 = 19 beats 12

scenes.narration: The last cell holds the best for the whole street: 19, from houses 1 and 4.
scenes.caption: The most without tripping an alarm: 19

scenes.narration: Every house is one choice: skip it and keep the previous best, or take it with the best from two back. One pass, O(n) time.
scenes.caption: Take or skip, using two answers already known
